36/S0.subgoal: Explain what contextual inquiry is, its active and passive modes, and why the observer must act as an apprentice rather than a teacher.

36/S1.subgoal: Describe the five stages of contextual inquiry and how the reflect stage uses affinity diagrams to analyze observed data.

36/S2.subgoal: Explain how the affinity diagram method organizes contextual inquiry notes into grouped design recommendations, using a note-taking application example, and distinguish those recommendations from implementation.

36/S3.subgoal: Demonstrate how affinity diagram grouping can be applied to calendar app observations to form reminder and scheduling requirement categories.

36/S4.subgoal: Summarize the lecture's coverage of contextual inquiry and affinity diagram analysis, and preview the next part on using the data for implementation.

goal.goal: Explain contextual inquiry and apply affinity diagrams to convert observed user behavior into usability requirements and design recommendations.
goal.achieves: This gives the learner a user-centered method for moving from requirement gathering to usability specification during XR system development.

objectives.goal: Explain how contextual inquiry is organized as a staged observational method, including active and passive modes, the master-apprentice observer stance, and reflection through affinity diagrams.
objectives.achieves: This lets the learner collect usability evidence from users in real task contexts and prepare that evidence for requirement-gathering work in an XR system development case study.

objectives.goal: Apply affinity diagrams to group contextual inquiry notes and observations into design recommendations and requirement categories while distinguishing requirements from implementation choices.
objectives.achieves: This lets the learner convert observed user needs into usable requirement specifications for later design and implementation of an XR system.
